newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: Greece keeps block on EU financial aid to Turkey.
newsitem.headline: Greece keeps block on EU financial aid to Turkey.

text.p: Greece on Tuesday maintained its long-standing veto on a European Union aid package to Turkey, dashing hopes in other EU states that Athens had had a change of heart.
EU ministers, however, were still planning to meet Turkish Foreign Minister Tansu Ciller later on Tuesday and to hold talks that have been put off since 1995.

Greek Foreign Minister Theodoros Pangalos said his country would participate in the meeting, but that it could not agree to unblock aid worth 375 million ecus ($424 million) until Turkey stopped threatening Greek sovereignty in the Aegean.
"We have repeatedly declared that we cannot accpet Turkish behaviour vis a vis out sovereignty," he told a news conference.
He said Turkey has to "withdraw the threat of war" over Greek plans to extend its maritime borders and must turn to international law to solve disputes in the region.
"We will continue in this firm position until we have satisfaction from the Turkish side," he said.
Greece and Turkey nearly came to war over a deserted islet in the Aegean Sea last year.
EU officials had earlier expressed hope that Greece was about to change its mind about the aid, which has been blocked since 1996.
The aid package had been promised to Ankara to help it meet the increased competition posed by the customs union which entered into force with the EU in January 1996.
In the absence of the aid Turkey says it has felt little benefit from the deal.
EU-Turkish relations were strained further earlier this year when mainly Christian Democratic politicians ruled out future Turkish membership of the EU because of cultural differences.
The bloc's foreign ministers later patched up the row by saying Turkey had a future in Europe.
Ciller was due in Luxembourg later to meet the EU ministers, but her plane made an emergency landing because of technical problems shortly after taking off from Istanbul.
The flight resumed, an official said.
